steps.say: The Weigert-Meyer law is taught routinely for duplex kidneys. The upper pole ureter is inserted inferomedially and ectopically. Upper pole obstruction is produced with ureterocele. The lower pole ureter is inserted superolaterally. Lower pole reflux is expected on voiding films. Both moieties are imaged separately for full clarity.
steps.tx: The **Weigert-Meyer law** (duplex plumbing rule) pairs each moiety with its fate: the upper pole ureter enters low and ectopic, inviting **upper pole obstruction** (blocked top kidney) with ureterocele, while the lower pole ureter enters high and sideways, inviting the classic **lower pole reflux** (leaky bottom kidney). Image both moieties separately, because one twin hides behind the other.

steps.say: Ureterocele is recognised as a cystic ureteral swelling. Intravesical ureterocele is confined within the bladder. Ectopic ureterocele is extended to the neck or urethra. Obstruction and infection are produced more by ectopic forms. The narrow neck is blamed for urinary trapping. Classification is recorded carefully before treatment planning.
steps.tx: A **ureterocele** (ballooned ureter end) is a cystic swelling of the terminal ureter, either **intravesical ureterocele** (inside bladder only, orthotopic) or **ectopic ureterocele** (spilling to neck or urethra). Ectopic forms obstruct and infect more, because the narrow neck traps urine.

steps.say: The cobra head sign is looked for on urography. A dense round defect is seen inside the full bladder. A thin pale halo is ringed around the defect. The spring onion sign is another name for the finding. Adequate bladder filling is required for display. Half empty studies are reported as non diagnostic.
steps.tx: The **cobra head sign** (snake head bulge), also called the **spring onion sign** (layered bulb), shows a dense round filling defect ringed by a pale halo inside a full bladder on urography. Fill the bladder well for the study, because a half empty bladder hides the halo.

steps.say: Endoscopic puncture is performed urgently as first decompression. Bugbee electrode cold knife or laser is selected according to availability. Obstructing ureteroceles are decompressed urgently in septic neonates. Puncture is placed low and medially. Continence is preserved by careful low siting. De novo reflux is watched for carefully afterwards.
steps.tx: **Endoscopic puncture** (keyhole pop) with Bugbee electrode, cold knife, or laser gives first **ureterocele decompression** (pressure release) for obstructing ureteroceles, especially septic neonates. Puncture low and medial to preserve continence, because high lateral cuts reflux. Reassess for de novo reflux afterwards and reimplant if persistent.

steps.say: Ectopic ureter in girls is suspected with constant dribbling. Openings beyond the sphincter are found in urethra or vagina. Continuous incontinence is reported despite normal voiding. Normal voiding is preserved from the healthy system. Wetness between toilet visits is described by mothers. Upper moiety bypass is confirmed on imaging.
steps.tx: In girls an **ectopic ureter female** (misplaced girl tube) can open beyond the sphincter into urethra, vagina, or vestibule, giving **continuous incontinence** (constant dribbling) despite **normal voiding** (regular toilet cycles). Believe the mother reporting wetness with normal voids, because the upper moiety bypasses control.

steps.say: Ectopic ureter in boys is always inserted above the sphincter. Posterior urethra and seminal passages are typical insertion sites. Incontinence is never caused by this male arrangement. Recurrent infection is investigated carefully instead. Epididymitis is seen commonly in adolescent presentations. Imaging is directed carefully at the seminal tract.
steps.tx: A boy's **ectopic ureter male** (misplaced boy tube) drains above the sphincter into posterior urethra, seminal vesicle, or ejaculatory duct, hence it **never causes incontinence** (no dribbling). Suspect it in recurrent infection or epididymitis without reflux, because pressure vents backward. Image the seminal tract when pus recurs without explanation.

steps.say: Heminephroureterectomy is offered for clearly non functioning moieties. Dysplastic upper pole is confirmed on DMSA scanning. Split function under 10 percent is documented. Laparoscopic or robotic excision is performed through small ports. Functioning tissue is preserved carefully whenever possible. Short stumps are left routinely to prevent later infection.
steps.tx: Remove dead moieties by laparoscopic or robotic **heminephroureterectomy** (upper pole excision) when split function falls under **10%** (ten) in a **dysplastic upper pole** (non working cap). Confirm with DMSA before cutting, because functioning tissue deserves preservation. Leave a ureteral stump short to avoid stump infections later.

steps.say: Ureteroureterostomy is performed cleanly when both moieties function. The blocked upper ureter is joined to the lower ureter. Moiety preservation is achieved without pelvic dissection. The join is stented briefly after careful surgery. Drainage is confirmed before stent removal. No kidney tissue is sacrificed at all by the repair.
steps.tx: **Ureteroureterostomy** (tube to tube join) sews the blocked upper ureter into the working lower ureter for true **moiety preservation** (kidney saving) without pelvic dissection. Choose it when both moieties function, because no kidney is lost. Stent the join briefly and confirm drainage before removal.
